top_signals.title: Ukraine’s Ground Robots and the Economics of Survival
top_signals.summary:
In August 2024, special forces from five Ukrainian military intelligence units crossed the Black Sea to raid Russian-held Kinburn Spit. The commandos of these units — Chimera, Aratta, Stuhna, Paragon, Terror, and the Siberian Battalion — landed, fought, destroyed equipment, and withdrew. Two years later, in July 2026, Ukraine returned, but left the soldiers behind. Instead, an uncrewed surface vessel carried a ground robot across the water and released it onto the shore. The robot, equipped with a Wolly 7.62 remotely operated combat module, featuring a machine gun and an AI-assisted targeting system, rolled onto shore and engaged targets. A

top_signals.title: Treasuries Rise After Fed’s Waller Notes Progress on Inflation
top_signals.summary: Treasuries rose after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be inclined to leave interest rates unchanged as long as inflation continues to slow.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: Trump’s Oil Deal Lifts Venezuela Bonds Ahead of Debt Rework
top_signals.summary: Venezuelan bonds have jumped since the Trump administration moved to take control of a huge swath of the country’s oil reserves, with investors factoring in the prospect of higher crude production as they await a debt restructuring that could top $200 billion.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.
